package_info.package_versions: Compromised versions published after npmjs account takeover (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised following an npm account takeover, resulting in the distribution of malicious code that exfiltrated users’ wallet data to an attacker-controlled domain. The malicious versions were published under the guise of the legitimate, high-reputation Ledger Connect Kit, targeting decentralized application users and enabling theft of cryptocurrency and sensitive wallet information.

execution_context.file_location: Main JavaScript bundle of Ledger Connect Kit (exact file name not specified in report)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code listens for the browser page load event, accesses wallet data from the user's browser context, and sends this data via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive wallet information and potential theft of cryptocurrency.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive wallet data and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled domain without user consent, which is a clear indicator of credential or asset theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Ledger Connect Kit should never transmit private wallet data or sensitive information to unknown third-party domains, especially without explicit user authorization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may send anonymized analytics or telemetry data to trusted, official domains, but never private keys, wallet contents, or sensitive user data to untrusted or hardcoded endpoints.
key_indicators: Network requests to hardcoded, untrusted domains within wallet-related code
Direct access to browser wallet APIs or DOM elements containing wallet data
Code injected or modified following a maintainer account compromise
Outbound HTTPS POST requests containing serialized wallet data

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises a former Ledger employee’s npmjs account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Gains ability to publish new versions of the Ledger Connect Kit package

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious versions of Ledger Connect Kit to npm under the legitimate package name.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users and projects unknowingly install the compromised package

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the user’s browser or application context, exfiltrating wallet data to an attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of cryptocurrency and sensitive wallet information from affected users

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in wallet-related npm packages making network requests to hardcoded or untrusted domains
Access to browser wallet APIs or DOM elements containing wallet data within package code
Unexpected or unauthorized code changes in high-reputation packages following maintainer account changes or suspicious publish activity
file_indicators: Modified or newly added main JavaScript bundle in Ledger Connect Kit
Presence of new, obfuscated, or suspicious code blocks making outbound network requests to unknown domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from wallet applications to domains not associated with Ledger or its official partners
Unusual traffic patterns from browser wallet extensions or dApps to previously unseen endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network requests originating from wallet-related JavaScript packages, especially after recent package updates or maintainer changes. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify code accessing wallet data and transmitting it to untrusted domains. Track package maintainer activity and flag sudden account changes or suspicious publishing behavior. Compare package versions for unauthorized code insertions or modifications, and alert on outbound requests to non-official domains.
